text:
maria: ran a quick nsys on the 70B pipeline with kv-prefetch enabled, noticing weird kernel coalescing around attention/kv cache boundaries. attaching the export: /nfs/profiles/1739512345.pkl :eyes:
jon: can you paste the top heatmap snippet?
alex: +1 to seeing the trace, but any chance the NVTX ranges are too coarse? we only have `batch:run` and `kernel:launch` today.
maria: pasted a small timeline excerpt:
```
[1739512346] NVTX: req:0/exec_start
[1739512346] NVTX: req:0/kv_prefetch
[1739512347] CUDA: kernel_attn_qkv (32ms)
[1739512360] NVTX: req:0/kv_apply
[1739512360] CUDA: kernel_kv_compress (4ms)
```
maria: you can see prefetch overlaps with big attn kernel, but nsys shows the big kernel split into two launches that get coalesced on the timeline, which hides the prefetch latency.
sam: hmm that sounds like kernel coalescing at the driver/hw level. when small kernels are back-to-back they merge in the timeline and NVTX ranges don't map 1:1.
jon: could be that our NVTX push/pop pairs aren't balanced for per-request spans. iirc we use a thread-local stack and sometimes we reuse range names which confuses grouping.
alex: proposal: add per-request scope prefix and sequence id in NVTX names, eg `req:<hexid>/span:<seq>/kv_prefetch`. keeps ranges unique and makes coalescing analysis easier.
maria: sounds good. also propose marking 'coalesce:allow' on short internal markers so we can intentionally tag ranges that shouldn't be analyzed as separate. not sure nvtx has that but we can annotate in metadata ranges.
perf-bot: automated note: sample run shows 42% of time in attention kernels, 8% in kv_prefetch, 10% in memcpy, remainder in small helpers. (run id 1739512345)
jon: practical question: adding unique per-request nvtx names will bloat trace logs — nsys UI slows with thousands of distinct ranges. is that acceptable?
sam: we can make it configurable (env var NVTX_REQ_GRANULARITY=none|coarse|per-request). default coarse so normal runs are cheap, per-request for targeted perfruns.
alex: also add a small synthetic test that forces kernel separation by inserting tiny 1us sleep between launches so nsys doesn't coalesce — useful as a regression harness.
maria: i ran nvprof/legacy and saw the same pattern. creating a short checklist for the change:
- add NVTX naming scheme: `req:<shortid>/span:<name>` (config toggle)
- ensure push/pop balanced in fast-path
- add internal marker `prefetch:hint` for KV prefetch ops
- add perf harness that toggles micro-sleeps to force separation
- run against 70B and 30B with and without coalescing
jon: i'll own the naming and config flag. alex can add the harness. maria can validate traces and update perf dashboard. sam will add a note in docs about the nsys UI overhead.
alex: quick nit: use base36 shortid (6 chars) to keep names compact.
maria: ok i'll open a PR with the nvtx helpers and a flag and attach a sample nsys slice to the PR for reviewers.
sam: ack. one more: can we also add an off-by-default tracer that emits compact JSON summary (start,end,name,reqid) to S3 so we can run large-scale traces without loading nsys UI?
perf-bot: reminder: keep trace retention <= 7d for full nsys exports per infra policy.
jon: agreed. thanks all — i'll create the issue and link the PR. :thumbsup:
